transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Potter. You were ordered to wait for backup. Instead you went in alone, blew out half a Muggle street, and a civilian is now in St. Mungo's with magical burns. Being the Boy Who Lived doesn't exempt you from protocol. What were you thinking?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I didn't expect it to go that far, ma'am. The Death Eater was about to apparate, and I thought if I could just catch him... I'm sorry for the property damage and the civilian. I should have followed orders.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Sorry" doesn't fix a Muggle street, Potter. You say you didn't expect it to go that far—that's exactly why we have protocols. Backup was three minutes out. Three minutes. You decided you knew better. Why?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It's just... when I see a Death Eater, it's like... it's like I can't help but chase them. It's the only way I know how to... to make sure they can't hurt anyone else. I'm sorry, I know I should have waited, but... I couldn't just let him get away.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: That's not good enough. You're an Auror now, not a vigilante. You think I don't understand the impulse? We all want to catch them. But we do it properly, or we end up with innocent people in St. Mungo's. Tell me—what exactly made you think your judgment was better than the entire department's operational plan?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You're right, ma'am. I... I don't know what I was thinking. It was just... habit, I guess. Reacting on instinct, without considering the consequences. I should have trusted the plan, trusted my team. It's... it's not an excuse, just... an explanation. I'm genuinely sorry for the damage and the injury. It was my mistake, and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Responsibility means more than just saying the words, Potter. It means facing the consequences. You're suspended for two weeks without pay, and you'll be assigned to assist the Obliviators in repairing the damage and memory-charming the Muggles involved. Every single one. Understood?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood, ma'am. I... I accept the consequences. It's the least I can do. I'll make sure every Muggle is taken care of, no matter how long it takes. I promise. Thank you for giving me the chance to... to fix what I did. I won't let you down.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: See that you don't. And Potter—next time, you wait for backup. That's not a suggestion. Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, ma'am. I'll remember that, I promise. Thank you for... for giving me another chance. I'll be in the office first thing in the morning, ready to start the memory charm work. Goodbye, ma'am.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good. I expect a full report on the Obliviation progress by the end of the week. Now get out of my office.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Of course, ma'am. I'll have the report ready by Friday. Thank you again. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods curtly, turning back to the paperwork on the desk.*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *Exits the office, closing the door behind him*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Sighs, pinching the bridge of her nose before returning to the stack of incident reports.*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *Harry makes his way down the hall, the weight of his mistake pressing heavily on his shoulders. He knows he's let down not only the department but also the people who trusted him to do the right thing.*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *After a moment, she stands and walks to the door, opening it slightly to watch him leave.* Potter. Don't make me regret this.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I won't, ma'am. I'll do whatever it takes to make up for this. Thank you for giving me another chance. I'll be... I'll be better, I promise.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: See that you are. Now go. The Obliviators are waiting.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, ma'am. I'll... I'll report to them immediately. Goodbye, ma'am.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He explains his actions as driven by instinct and habit, showing limited reflection on alternative approaches beyond his own impulsive reaction.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He admits to ignoring protocols and operational plans, acting on impulse without considering consequences, leading to severe collateral damage.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He is deferential and apologetic in the confrontation, showing no assertive or dominant behavior; he accepts blame and instructions passively.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He repeatedly apologizes, accepts full responsibility, and promises to make amends, showing high concern for others affected by his actions.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He expresses heavy guilt ('weight of his mistake pressing heavily'), shows anxiety about letting people down, and seeks reassurance.
